messages:
Laura: quick check — i'm seeing a ~12% latency regression when we enable structured-output + function-call wrapping in streaming. can someone run a focused bench and confirm? seq=512, tokens out ~256.
Anil: i can run something on a dev node in a bit. which model/image and exact config?
Laura: use rwd/bench:latest, model=redwood-v1-8b-qat, batch=8, concurrency=16, seq_in=512, gen=256. compare 3 runs: (a) streaming plain text, (b) streaming with function-call metadata + schema, (c) non-streaming function-call.
Mike: fyi runtime 0.9.3 added the JSON schema validator hook — that may add CPU in the postprocess path. could be the culprit. :eyes:
Sasha: also add a run with `--disable-postprocess-hook` to isolate it. and please capture p99 p50 p95 and token/sec.
Laura: good call. also log `kv-cache` hit metrics and cpu profile. upload perf artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/1779823456/
Anil: running now. here's the command i'm using:
```bash
./rwd-bench --image rwd/bench:latest \
  --model redwood-v1-8b-qat \
  --seq 512 --gen 256 --batch 8 --concurrency 16 \
  --modes streaming,streaming+funcschema,nonstream-func \
  --trace cpu,kvcache,latency --out-dir /tmp/bench-1779823456
```
Katie: adding me as a follow-up owner for collecting traces and uploading. will look at traces once Anil posts them. :thumbsup:
Anil: initial results (warm run, single node):
- streaming plain: p50 38ms/token, p95 72ms/token, token/sec 720
- streaming+funcschema: p50 43ms/token, p95 86ms/token, token/sec 610
- nonstream-func: p50 46ms/token, p95 90ms/token, token/sec 580
These are with postprocess hook enabled. cpu shows a spike in python postprocess at function-call finalize step.
Sasha: that's larger than expected. can you re-run with `--disable-postprocess-hook` and with `PY_PROFILE=1` env so we get line-level CPU?
Anil: re-run kicked off; ETA ~6m.
PerfBot: automated note: benchmark started by Anil at 1779823560, run id bench-1779823560. will post summary when complete.
Laura: thanks — if the postprocess hook is the issue we should patch the runtime to do schema validation async or in a lightweight C path. filing a follow-up if confirmed.
Anil: second run (hook disabled): streaming+funcschema p50 39ms/token, p95 74ms/token, token/sec 700. cpu profile attached to /tmp/bench-1779823456/profile.json (uploading now).
Katie: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/1779823456/artifacts.zip and linked a flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.ai/flame/1779823456
Mike: looking at flamegraph — ~60% of extra time is in jsonschema.validate in python. we should move schema validation into the C postprocess or pre-compile validators. low-risk fix: cache compiled validators per-schema id.
Sasha: agree. also add a tiny unit that skips validation if request includes `x-skip-schema: true` for internal traffic.
Laura: ok owners: Anil will open the bench PR with repro steps + artifacts, Mike will prototype compiled-validator cache, Sasha will add header gate + tests, Katie will coordinate rollout canary. i'll create the tracking task.
Anil: PR link coming shortly. perf bot will post final automated summary when it's done.
PerfBot: benchmark completed at 1779823680 — summary: regression attributable to python schema validation; disable/optimize yields parity with baseline. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/1779823456/artifacts.zip
Laura: great — thanks all. we'll prioritize a patch and plan a canary for runtime 0.9.4.
